content: Nicorette is a branded over-the-counter treatment designed to alleviate the withdrawal symptoms associated with smoking cessation. Initially developed as part of Pfizer Consumer Healthcare Products, the brand was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2006. The product was originally introduced as a transdermal patch for topical application but later expanded to include nicotine gum (containing nicotine polacrilex), lozenges, inhalers, and nasal sprays. All these formulations contain nicotine as the active ingredient, which is delivered into the bloodstream to help manage cravings and withdrawal symptoms. These products are collectively referred to as nicotine replacement therapies (NRTs). Alternative brand names for similar nicotine replacement products include Prostep, Habitrol, Nicotrol, Nicoderm, and Commit. Commit lozenges, in particular, are an oral aid designed to support individuals in quitting smoking. They are available in two dosages: 4 mg for individuals who smoke their first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking and 2 mg for those who wait longer than 30 minutes before their first nicotine intake. The lozenges, which are mint-flavored, are intended to be taken orally at least nine times per day during the first two weeks after a person decides to quit using tobacco products. Nicorette inhalers are widely available over the counter in many regions. However, in the United States, they are marketed under the brand name Nicotrol Inhalers and are only available with a prescription. It is generally recommended to discontinue the use of Nicorette products after 12 weeks, as prolonged use or misuse can lead to nicotine dependence, similar to smoking. Additionally, online searches may reveal international or Canadian retailers offering these products at significantly reduced prices, often shipping to the United States for half the cost.
